def-volume-integral-scattering-model:
## Definition

Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable set, let $M:=|D|$, let $q\in L^\infty(D;\mathbb C)$, and let $k\in\mathbb R$. Here $L^2$ and $L^\infty$ are equivalence classes modulo null functions ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and $L^\infty$ means essentially bounded with respect to Lebesgue measure ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]). We regard $q$ as zero off $D$. The convention is the volume equation
$$u=f+K_k u,\qquad K_k u(x):=\int_D G_k(x-y)q(y)u(y)\,dy,\qquad G_k(z):=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|}\quad(z\ne0).$$
Set $G_k(0):=0$; when $M>0$ the diagonal in $D\times D$ is product-null, so this value is only a representative convention. The input and unknown are classes in complex $L^2(D)$, and the displayed equation is interpreted as an equality of those classes. Its formula is well defined by [[lem-volume-integral-operator-well-defined-and-bounded]].

The associated far-field map is
$$\mathcal F_k[v](\theta):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_D e^{-ik\theta\cdot y}q(y)v(y)\,dy,\qquad \theta\in S^2.$$
Here $S^2$ has the surface measure of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. The map is well defined as a continuous function of $\theta$ by [[lem-volume-far-field-map-is-bounded]].

For $x\notin\overline D$, the exterior volume potential is
$$V_kv(x):=\int_D G_k(x-y)q(y)v(y)\,dy.$$
This is absolutely convergent because $x$ has positive distance from the compact set $\overline D$ and $qv\in L^1(D)$.

If $M=0$, define $L^2(D)=\{0\}$ and $K_k=0$; all solution and far-field statements on that space are the zero-space statements. The substantive operator results below assume $0<M<\infty$.

This is a stipulated integral-equation model with the sign convention $(-\Delta-k^2)(u-f)=q u$ when the corresponding distributional Helmholtz equation is used. In the acoustic notation of Scherzer–Mindrinos, their equation $u=u_i-k^2\Phi*((1-n)u)$ corresponds to $q=k^2(n-1)$. No existence or uniqueness for all contrasts is asserted by this definition.
lem-finite-volume-hilbert-schmidt-rescal:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $(X,\mu)$ and $(Y,
u)$ be finite measure spaces with masses $0<M_X:=\mu(X)<\infty$ and $0<M_Y:=
u(Y)<\infty$. Put $d\widehat\mu=d\mu/M_X$ and $d\widehat
u=d
u/M_Y$. For $a\in L^2(X	imes Y,\mu	imes
u)$, let $T_a:L^2(Y,
u)	o L^2(X,\mu)$ be its square-integrable-kernel operator and let $\widehat T$ be the operator with kernel $\widehat a:=\sqrt{M_XM_Y}\,a$ against $\widehat
u$. The maps $U_Xg=\sqrt{M_X}g$ and $U_Yh=\sqrt{M_Y}h$ are unitary and
$$U_XT_aU_Y^{-1}=\widehat T.$$
Moreover $\|\widehat a\|_{L^2(\widehat\mu	imes\widehat
u)}=\|a\|_{L^2(\mu	imes
u)}$, so the operator norms and kernel $L^2$ norms agree. If either mass is zero, the corresponding $L^2$ space and kernel operator are zero.

For $X=Y=D$ with Lebesgue mass $M>0$, the normalized kernel is $\widehat a=Ma$ and the measure is $d\widehat x=dx/M$.
lem-three-dimensional-scattering-kernel-:
## Statement

Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and Lebesgue measurable, let $M:=|D|$, $d_D:=\operatorname{diam}(D)$, $q\in L^\infty(D;\mathbb C)$, and $k\in\mathbb R$. If $M>0$, define $a(x,y)=G_k(x-y)q(y)$ off the diagonal and set it to zero on the diagonal. Then $a\in L^2(D\times D)$ and
$$\|a\|_{L^2(D\times D)}^2\le\frac{\|q\|_\infty^2 M d_D}{4\pi}.$$
If $M=0$, every measurable kernel on $D\times D$ represents the zero product $L^2$ class.
lem-volume-integral-operator-well-define:
## Statement

Let $D$ have finite Lebesgue measure. For every product-measurable kernel $a\in L^2(D\times D;\mathbb C)$, the formula $T_av(x)=\int_Da(x,y)v(y)dy$ defines a representative-independent complex-linear map $L^2(D;\mathbb C)\to L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ and $\|T_a\|\le\|a\|_{L^2(D\times D)}$. Consequently, under [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$,
$$\|K_k\|_{L^2\to L^2}\le\|G_k(\cdot-\cdot)q(\cdot)\|_{L^2(D\times D)}\le\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{\frac{|D|\,\operatorname{diam}(D)}{4\pi}}.$$
For $|D|=0$ the operator is zero.
thm-volume-integral-operator-is-compact:
## Statement

Assume AC and the data of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$. Then $K_k:L^2(D;\mathbb C)\to L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ is compact and
$$\|K_k\|\le\|G_k(x-y)q(y)\|_{L^2(D\times D)}\le\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{\frac{|D|\operatorname{diam}(D)}{4\pi}}.$$

The proof supplies both the finite-measure Hilbert–Schmidt rescaling route required by the kernel interface and the singular-truncation/Schur route specified for this volume kernel. No uniqueness or outgoing-scattering solvability is asserted here.
thm-volume-integral-scattering-born-neum:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the data of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$. If $\rho:=\|K_k\|_{L^2\to L^2}<1$, then for every $f\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ the equation $u=f+K_ku$ has a unique solution. For each integer $m\ge0$, define the Born partial sum $u_m:=\sum_{j=0}^{m}K_k^jf$. Then
$$\|u-u_m\|_2\le\frac{\rho^{m+1}}{1-\rho}\|f\|_2.$$
No compactness, analytic continuation, or physical uniqueness hypothesis is used in this small-norm branch.
thm-volume-integral-scattering-fredholm-:
## Statement

Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$. If $K_k$ is injective through $I-K_k$, then for every $f\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ there is a unique $u\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ solving $(I-K_k)u=f$, and $A_k:=I-K_k$ has a bounded inverse. Writing $R_k:=\|A_k^{-1}\|$, every $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ satisfies
$$\|u-v\|_2\le R_k\|f-(I-K_k)v\|_2.$$
This is an operator-theoretic Fredholm branch; no physical uniqueness statement for the exterior PDE is asserted.
lem-volume-far-field-map-is-bounded:
## Statement

Let $D,q,k$ be as in [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]], with $0<|D|<\infty$, and put $R_0>\sup_{y\in D}|y|$. Then $\mathcal F_k:L^2(D;\mathbb C)\to C(S^2;\mathbb C)$ is linear and
$$\|\mathcal F_kv\|_\infty\le\frac{\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{|D|}}{4\pi}\|v\|_2.$$
It is Lipschitz in direction with constant at most $|k|R_0\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{|D|}\|v\|_2/(4\pi)$. For every $r\ge2R_0$, the exterior volume potential of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] satisfies
$$\sup_{\theta\in S^2}\left|r e^{-ikr}V_kv(r\theta)-\mathcal F_kv(\theta)\right|\le\frac{2R_0+|k|R_0^2}{4\pi r}\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{|D|}\|v\|_2.$$
Thus $\mathcal F_kv$ is the uniform far-field amplitude under the outgoing $e^{ikr}/r$ convention.
lem-dyadic-cell-average-projections-conv:
## Statement

Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and Lebesgue measurable, and choose a half-open cube $Q$ containing $D$. Subdivide $Q$ into its nested dyadic cubes at mesh $h_N=2^{-N}\operatorname{side}(Q)$. Let $E_{N,j}=D\cap Q_{N,j}$ range over the finitely many cells of positive measure, let $V_N\subset L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ be the functions constant on each such cell, and define $P_N$ by replacing a function on each $E_{N,j}$ by its cell average. Then $P_N$ is the orthogonal projection onto $V_N$, $\|P_N\|\le1$, the spaces $V_N$ are increasing, and $P_Nv\to v$ in $L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ for every $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$.
def-volume-product-integration-scheme:
## Definition

Let $D,q,k$ be as in [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]], $0<|D|<\infty$, let $P_N$ be the dyadic cell-average projection of [[lem-dyadic-cell-average-projections-converge-in-l2]], and put $K_N:=P_NK_k$ and $f_N:=P_Nf$. This is a finite-rank volume product-integration rule on $L^2(D)$; the projection and kernel convention are fixed by those definitions.

For each positive-measure cell $E_{N,j}$ set $\phi_{N,j}:=|E_{N,j}|^{-1/2}\mathbf1_{E_{N,j}}$. The exact product-cell weights and right-hand side are
$$A^{(N)}_{ij}:=\langle K_k\phi_{N,j},\phi_{N,i}\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|E_{N,i}||E_{N,j}|}}\int_{E_{N,i}}\int_{E_{N,j}}G_k(x-y)q(y)\,dy\,dx,\qquad b^{(N)}_i:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|E_{N,i}|}}\int_{E_{N,i}}f(x)\,dx.$$
The finite system is $(I-A^{(N)})c=b^{(N)}$, and its reconstruction is $u_N=\sum_jc_j\phi_{N,j}$. Equivalently, it solves $(I-K_N)u_N=f_N$ in $V_N$. Its far-field output is the exact cell integral
$$\mathcal F_N(c)(\theta):=\mathcal F_k[u_N](\theta)=\sum_j\frac{c_j}{4\pi\sqrt{|E_{N,j}|}}\int_{E_{N,j}}e^{-ik\theta\cdot y}q(y)\,dy.$$
A singular finite matrix has status `singular`; the definition makes no unconditional invertibility claim. The double integrals are taken over whole cell pairs, including diagonal pairs; no point value of $G_k$ at its singular diagonal is sampled. Finiteness is established by [[lem-volume-integral-operator-well-defined-and-bounded]] and [[lem-volume-far-field-map-is-bounded]].

The rule uses exact cell weights as a mathematical discretization. This definition makes no claim about floating-point evaluation or approximate cell weights.
thm-volume-product-integration-solution-:
## Statement

Assume AC and the data of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$. Let $P_N,K_N=P_NK_k,f_N=P_Nf$ and the exact cell-pair matrices be as in [[def-volume-product-integration-scheme]], and suppose $I-K_k$ is injective. Then there is $N_0$ such that for all $N\ge N_0$ the matrix $I-A^{(N)}$ is nonsingular and its reconstruction $u_N\in V_N$ is the unique solution of $(I-K_N)u_N=f_N$. If $u$ solves $(I-K_k)u=f$, there is a constant $C<\infty$ independent of $N,f$ such that
$$\|u_N-u\|_2\le C\bigl(\|(P_N-I)K_ku\|_2+\|(P_N-I)f\|_2\bigr).$$
Writing $C_F:=\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{|D|}/(4\pi)$, the exact far-field outputs obey
$$\|\mathcal F_k[u_N]-\mathcal F_k[u]\|_{C(S^2)}\le C_F C\bigl(\|(P_N-I)K_ku\|_2+\|(P_N-I)f\|_2\bigr)\longrightarrow0.$$
This gives eventual solvability and convergence for the stated cell-volume product rule; it does not assert operator-norm convergence $K_N\to K_k$ or finite-precision error bounds.
def-spherical-harmonic-partial-wave-conv:
## Definition

Use the unit sphere $S^2$ and its polar surface measure $d\sigma$ from [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. For each integer $\ell\ge0$, let $\mathcal H_\ell$ be the complex vector space of restrictions to $S^2$ of homogeneous degree-$\ell$ polynomials $P$ on $\mathbb R^3$ satisfying the Euclidean harmonic equation $\Delta P=0$. In polar coordinates $x=r\omega$, define $\Delta_{S^2}$ by
$$\Delta_{\mathbb R^3}=\partial_r^2+\frac2r\partial_r+\frac1{r^2}\Delta_{S^2},$$
equivalently $\Delta_{S^2}=\frac1{\sin\theta}\partial_\theta(\sin\theta\partial_\theta)+\frac1{\sin^2\theta}\partial_\phi^2$ away from the poles. Thus if $Y\in\mathcal H_\ell$ is the restriction of $P$, then $\Delta_{S^2}Y=-\ell(\ell+1)Y$.

For $\ell\ge0$, define the normalized zonal polynomial $P_\ell(t)$ to be the degree-$\ell$ polynomial satisfying
$$ (1-t^2)P_\ell''(t)-2tP_\ell'(t)+\ell(\ell+1)P_\ell(t)=0,\qquad P_\ell(1)=1.$$
The later harmonic-basis lemma proves existence and uniqueness of this normalized polynomial and identifies it with the usual Legendre convention.

The term **partial wave of degree $\ell$** means the $\mathcal H_\ell$ component of an angular expansion in $L^2(S^2,d\sigma;\mathbb C)$. Completeness, orthogonality, finite dimension, and the evaluation bound for these components are established in [[lem-spherical-harmonics-form-complete-basis-and-addition-formula]].

For a radial field $u(r,\omega)$, its degree-$\ell$ component is written $u_\ell(r,\omega)\in\mathcal H_\ell$; any orthonormal basis within this finite-dimensional space gives the equivalent scalar mode equations. The definition does not select such a basis globally.
lem-spherical-harmonics-form-complete-ba:
## Statement

Use $\mathcal H_\ell$ from [[def-spherical-harmonic-partial-wave-conventions]]. For every $\ell\ge0$, $\dim_\mathbb C\mathcal H_\ell=2\ell+1$; the spaces $\mathcal H_\ell$ are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2(S^2,d\sigma;\mathbb C)$ and their algebraic sum is dense there. Thus they give a complete orthogonal spherical-harmonic expansion. For any orthonormal basis $Y_{\ell 1},\ldots,Y_{\ell,2\ell+1}$ of $\mathcal H_\ell$, the basis-independent reproducing kernel
$$Z_\ell(\omega,\eta):=\sum_{m=1}^{2\ell+1}Y_{\ell m}(\omega)\overline{Y_{\ell m}(\eta)}$$
satisfies $Z_\ell(\omega,\omega)=(2\ell+1)/(4\pi)$. In particular,
$$|g(\omega)|\le\sqrt{\frac{2\ell+1}{4\pi}}\,\|g\|_{L^2(S^2)}\qquad(g\in\mathcal H_\ell).$$
For fixed $\eta$, rotational invariance makes $Z_\ell(\omega,\eta)$ a degree-$\ell$ zonal polynomial of $\omega\cdot\eta$; normalizing $P_\ell(1)=1$ gives the usual addition identity $Z_\ell(\omega,\eta)=\frac{2\ell+1}{4\pi}P_\ell(\omega\cdot\eta)$.
lem-outgoing-helmholtz-kernel-is-a-funda:
## Statement

For real $k$, let $\Phi_k(x)=e^{ik|x|}/(4\pi|x|)$ for $x\ne0$. In the sense of distributions on $\mathbb R^3$,
$$(-\Delta-k^2)\Phi_k=\delta_0.$$
Here $\delta_0$ is the point-mass distribution defined by $\langle\delta_0,\varphi\rangle=\varphi(0)$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$. Consequently, if $g\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ has bounded support, the integral $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Phi_k(x-y)g(y)\,dy$ is absolutely finite for almost every $x$. Define $V$ by this integral almost everywhere (and arbitrarily on the exceptional null set). Then $V\in L^1_{\rm loc}$ and $(-\Delta-k^2)V=g$ distributionally.
thm-volume-scattering-radial-partial-wav:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $R>0$, $k>0$, and $Q\in C([0,R];\mathbb C)$. Set $q(x)=Q(|x|)$ on $B_R$ and $q(x)=0$ outside $B_R$. Choose for every $\ell$ an orthonormal basis $Y_{\ell m}$ of $\mathcal H_\ell$. Suppose $u^{\rm inc}$ is a classical free Helmholtz field and $u=u^{\rm inc}+V$ satisfies the volume-potential equation $V(x)=\int_{B_R}G_k(x-y)q(y)u(y)dy$. Assume $u$ is continuous on $\overline B_R$, piecewise $C^2$ on either side of $|x|=R$, and $u$ and its radial derivative are continuous across that interface. For every spherical harmonic $Y_{\ell m}$ assume its coefficient
$$w_{\ell m}(r):=r\int_{S^2}u(r\omega)\overline{Y_{\ell m}(\omega)}d\sigma(\omega)$$
satisfies the regular-origin condition $w_{\ell m}(r)=O(r^{\ell+1})$ as $r\downarrow0$. Write the incident mode as $r\int u^{\rm inc}(r\omega)\overline{Y_{\ell m}}d\sigma=\alpha_{\ell m}rj_\ell(kr)$. The outgoing radiation condition is $\lim_{r\to\infty}\sup_{\omega\in S^2}|r(\partial_rV(r\omega)-ikV(r\omega))|=0$. Then each reduced mode satisfies
$$w_{\ell m}''(r)+\left(k^2+Q(r)-\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{r^2}\right)w_{\ell m}(r)=0\quad(0<r<R),$$
is regular at $0$, and has for $r>R$ the form
$$w_{\ell m}(r)=\alpha_{\ell m}rj_\ell(kr)+\beta_{\ell m}rh_\ell^{(1)}(kr).$$
The interior and exterior values and first derivatives agree at $R$. This is a conditional mode reduction and matching statement; it asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of the total field.
thm-exponential-partial-wave-truncation-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $b_\ell\in\mathcal H_\ell$ for every integer $\ell\ge0$, where $\mathcal H_\ell$ is defined in [[def-spherical-harmonic-partial-wave-conventions]]. Suppose constants $C\ge0$ and $\rho>1$ satisfy $\|b_\ell\|_{L^2(S^2)}\le C\rho^{-\ell}$ for all $\ell$. Then $b(\omega):=\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty b_\ell(\omega)$ converges uniformly on $S^2$, and for every integer $L\ge0$,
$$\sup_{\omega\in S^2}\left|b(\omega)-\sum_{\ell=0}^L b_\ell(\omega)\right|\le C\sqrt{\frac{2L+3}{4\pi}}\,\frac{\rho^{-(L+1)}}{(1-\rho^{-1})^2}.$$
This is a conditional angular-coefficient bound; it does not assert exponential decay for general scattering data.
